strategy.thesis: Corporate VC arm of KB Financial Group; one of Korea's largest and oldest VCs, investing across ICT, AI, deep-tech and bio with KB group affiliates participating as LPs.

summary.en: KB Investment is the corporate venture capital arm of KB Financial Group, Korea's largest financial holding company. Founded in March 1990 (originally Jang-Eun Venture Capital), it is one of Korea's oldest and largest VCs, with ~327 portfolio investments across 63 funds and a focus on AI, deep-tech, semiconductors, bio/healthcare and enterprise. KB group affiliates act as LPs, including in its KRW 250bn Global Platform Fund 2.

funds.name: TGC Square (SK TGC Square, Singapore semiconductor VC vehicle)

size.raw: Over KRW 100bn co-invested with SK Hynix, Shinhan Financial Group, LIG Nex1 et al.

strategy.thesis: Investment holding company spun off from SK Telecom in 2021 to invest in semiconductor and ICT; functions as SK Telecom lineage's CVC vehicle, including the Singapore-based SK TGC Square fund targeting AI-semiconductor and materials/parts/equipment firms in the US and Japan.

summary.en: SK Square is the investment holding company spun off from SK Telecom on Nov 1, 2021 to enable semiconductor and ICT investment (after holding-company-law constraints limited SK Telecom's direct CVC activity). It acts as the SK Telecom lineage's de-facto CVC arm, co-establishing the Singapore-based SK TGC Square fund (KRW 100bn+) with SK Hynix, Shinhan Financial Group and others to invest in AI-semiconductor and chip materials/parts/equipment companies in the US and Japan.

strategy.thesis: CVC of POSCO Holdings, investing via Holdings CVC, cooperative CVC and proprietary investment (PI) to balance the group's core strategic areas, strategy-adjacent areas and promising future sectors — with a turn toward eco-friendly/secondary-battery and green investments.

summary.en: POSCO Technology Investment is the corporate VC of POSCO Holdings, established June 1997 (initial capital KRW 10bn, POSCO 100%). With current capital of KRW 103.7bn and ~KRW 1.1tn AUM, it invests through Holdings CVC, cooperative CVC and proprietary investment across the group's core strategic, strategy-adjacent and future sectors, increasingly emphasizing eco-friendly, secondary-battery and energy-transition startups. Offices in Seoul and Pohang.

summary.local: 한화 드림플러스는 한화생명의 오픈이노베이션 브랜드이자 기업형 액셀러레이터·CVC 플랫폼이다. '한화생명 드림플러스 63 핀테크센터'는 2016년 10월 개관, 국내 최대 핀테크 스타트업 육성기관이자 보험사 최초의 핀테크 지원센터다. 드림플러스 강남은 대규모 코워킹 캠퍼스로, 입주사에 무료 사무공간(기본 6개월)·액셀러레이팅·파트너십·투자유치를 지원하며 한화자산운용이 2017년부터 벤처투자를 해왔다.

sources.supports: Dream Plus 63 opening Oct 2016, largest fintech nurturing institution, twice-yearly recruitment, free space
sources.quote: 'Hanwha Life Dream Plus 63 Fintech Center' opened in October 2016 and is the largest fintech startup nurturing institution in Korea and the first fintech support center among domestic insurance companies... recruiting resident companies twice a year through an open call process, offering free office space and facilities for a basic 6-month period

sources.quote: Hanwha Asset Management, which began venture investment in 2017, made its first official public announcement of its VC investment strategy

verification_notes: DreamPlus is an open-innovation/accelerator brand of Hanwha Life rather than a standalone licensed VC; Hanwha's direct VC investing is via Hanwha Asset Management (since 2017). Classified as CVC with accelerator/incubator subtypes. Program-level economics (equity %, ticket sizes) not disclosed in fetched sources, left null. The defunct Hanwha Investment (한화인베스트먼트, 2000-2020) is excluded as inactive.
